August 8, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Tang Sung (党声) (Party Voice) published the following
article on July 27:-

THE THREE DEMANDS OF THE FOREIGN RESIDENTS' FEDERATION

Recently the Shanghai Foreign Residents'
Federation submitted the following three demands to
the Settlement Authorities:-
1) That all new and cheap methods of
communication be encouraged, such as street motor-
cars or taxis, and that the number of policemen directing
traffic be increased.
2) That the number of ricshas be reduced
by at least 10%.
3) That efforts be made to reduce street
noises and that hawkers be not allowed to cry out their
wares or to create noise by other means.
A section of the Chinese residents may agree
with a part of these demands but if the whole body of
Chinese residents were to be asked to suggest improvements
in the municipal administration, their proposals would
be different from those of the foreigners. Chinese
residents would desire more important improvements and
as no important improvements have yet been carried out,
the time has not come to set forth secondary demands
such as those suggested by the foreign residents.
At present many coolies sleep on the
street during the night owing to the heat in their
quarters, usually a small room or a loft. In the
eyes of Chinese residents the housing problem is of far
more importance than street noises or the improvement of
traffic in the Settlements. Unless they can sleep
with some comfort in their houses, Chinese will not pay
much attention to street noises. The opinion of the
foreign residents is really the opinion of that section
of people who are enjoying a comfortable living.
We hope that the Settlement Authorities will
consider first the welfare of the Chinese ratepayers
who are in a majority.

Tang Sung (Party Voice) published the following article on
July 27:-

THE INCREASE IN THE HAND TROLLEY LICENCE FEE

Recently the S.M.C. decided to increase the
licence fees of hand trolleys. The hand trolley owners
and pullers then detailed representatives to appeal to
the S.M.C. for the cancellation of the increase on the
ground that owing to the trade depression they are unable
to bear any increase in the licence fee.
The present licence fee is $2.50 per quarter
but if the increase is passed it will be $5.00 per quarter.
There are altogether about 12,000 hand trolleys in
Shanghai and more than 100,000 persons are earning a
living as pullers.
It is a social problem which calls for
careful handling. We hope that the Settlement Authorities
will deal with it in a careful manner because it affects
the livelihood of more than 100,000 persons.

1935年8月8日。下午译文。

《党声》于7月27日刊登了以下文章：-

外籍居民联合会的三项要求

近日，上海外籍居民联合会向租界当局提交了以下三项要求：-
1) 鼓励所有新型且廉价的交通方式，如街道汽车或出租车，并增加指挥交通的警察人数。
2) 人力车数量至少减少10%。
3) 努力减少街道噪音，禁止小贩叫卖货物或以其他方式制造噪音。
部分中国居民可能同意这些要求中的一部分，但如果请全体中国居民就市政管理的改进提出建议，他们的提议将与外国人的不同。中国居民希望进行更重要的改进，既然尚未实施任何重要改进，现在还不是提出像外籍居民所建议的那些次要要求的时候。
目前，由于住所（通常是一间小房间或阁楼）炎热，许多苦力夜间睡在街上。在中国居民看来，住房问题远比租界的街道噪音或交通改善重要得多。除非他们能在家里睡得稍微舒适些，否则中国人不会太关注街道噪音。外籍居民的意见实际上是那些生活舒适的人的意见。
我们希望租界当局首先考虑占多数的中国纳税人的福利。

《党声》于7月27日刊登了以下文章：-

手推车执照费的增加

近日，工部局决定提高手推车的执照费。手推车车主和拉车夫随后派出代表向工部局申诉，要求取消加价，理由是鉴于商业萧条，他们无力承担任何执照费的增加。
目前的执照费为每季度2.50元，但如果加价通过，将变为每季度5.00元。
上海共有手推车约12,000辆，超过10万人以拉车为生。
这是一个需要谨慎处理的社会问题。我们希望租界当局能谨慎处理此事，因为它关系到超过10万人的生计。

2 November 23, 1933 SHANGHAI CA
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S.-P. REC'D
A REPLY TO BOB BRYAN AND THE
SHANGHAI RESIDENTS ASSOCIATION
By F. C. MILLINGTON.
Date / /

THINGS ARE looking up. People are actually beginning to take an interest in broadcasting, and even Associations are sitting up and taking notice. Doesn't this put heart into the folk who have been striving to accomplish something in this direction for the past two years and most of the time, apparently, playing a very lone game.

However, here we have complaints from both Mr. Bryan and the Secretary of the Foreign Residents Association and I feel certain that this will lead eventually to action. People of the calibre of Mr. Woodhead, Mr. Harris and Mr. R. G. McDonald seldom set their hands to any plough without things happening in the long run and it is with a certain amount of pleasure and satisfaction that I read a second letter addressed to myself after the one received by Mr. Marshall had been answered. In another part of this issue will be found the letter and the reply there to and it now behoves someone to make a few suggestions as to what might be done.

We could, of course boost up the power of XCBL (I give it this name so that Bob may recognise it....its official title is now XQHC and though it took me the best part of two months to get the letters in their right order I now know them off by heart without having to turn up the Programme page of 'Shanghai Calling') to anything from one to five kilowatts but that would require capital and as the Company running the station has sunk something like one hundred thousand dollars into the station it doesn't feel inclined to sink anymore. If the foreign residents of Shanghai would only come along with their $10 annual subscription to help entertain themselves THEN something in this direction WOULD be done but so few of them think of sending in their annual fee that it is mighty difficult to make both ends meet let alone in more plant and machinery to give the required boost to the transmitter. Why cannot the Foreign Residents Association get every member in their Association who owns a radio set become a member of the China Broadcast Association and so help along something they will miss very badly if through some mischance the whole station has to close through lack of such support? There might come a time when a broadcasting station might be very useful in time of trouble Newspapers might go on strike or trouble might break out at a most inopportune moment and THEN where should we be without a foreign radio station Those of you who were home during the general strike in 1926 will no doubt remember how radio kept the public in good humour, kept them informed as to the latest news of what was happening all over the country, enabled Mr. Baldwin to talk to the whole nation and so settled the nerves of a goodly number of very perturbed people. One day we shall all be very grateful to some radio station here, although I for one, hope the occasion may not arise. Therefore I say, support the C.B.A. and help XCBL to get a little more power to its elbow.

Another way, Bob, if you wish to get good reception of XQHC why not buy a Philco....now like you....I have no Philco axe to grind. I merely state this because I am picking up XQHC on this little set quite distinctly and clearly each evening and throughout the day, without any interference whatsoever. And I have already told you that my British set would not do it.

Incidentally things are moving in the situation of the foreign broadcasting stations in Shanghai. All kinds of schemes are on foot to improve the position but I am not at liberty either to discuss them or to make any comments one way or the other. Something is bound to come of them though exactly what I cannot say.

If the Shanghai Foreign Residents Association take the matter in hand there is no doubt that our Chinese friends will endeavour to make the offending stations keep on their own wave band. The trouble is there is no central control of stations yet. There ought to be and the police of all settlements should be allowed to go straight to the offending station and close it down until it got on to its proper band. The rule states, I believe, that no station should be within 20 kilocycles of any other station and if this rule were kept everything in the garden or air would be lovely. Unfortunately stations do not have knife edge tuning and hence some of them cover 20 to 50 kilocycles on some sets and this makes good reception impossible. When crystal control is insisted upon again trouble will go, but it all depends on getting some central control. Could the Association not obtain personal contact with the men in power at Nanking and Shanghai, get them to meet and have them create a controlling body which would have the power to close offending stations for a week at a time or even longer, until they came into line, and until this is done by someone there will be trouble in the air. Isn't that something worth putting on the agenda for the meeting next week?

Unfortunately I am not a technician so I cannot make concrete suggestions, but there are many men in Shanghai who are quite capable of doing this. Bayliss worked like a nigger on the business. Now he has gone I would suggest the engineers of the various stations be asked to draw up a memorandum on the subject to be submitted to the forthcoming meeting. I feel sure Mr. Parks, Mr. Guerin, and John Marshall could very easily make suggestions that would have very far reaching results, BUT unless there is unified control suggestions are useless and THAT is the problem that has to be settled.

Shanghai Foreign Residents... IT IS UP TO YOU if you want things done, remember the motto DO IT YOURSELF and the whole city will thank you both Chinese and foreign residents.

One final word. Unless the Chinese authorities are consulted and brought into complete sympathy with any scheme that is suggested complete failure will, I am sure, result.

2 1933年11月23日 上海CA
上海公共租界
C. & S.-P. 收悉
致鲍勃·布莱恩及上海居民协会的回复
作者：F. C. MILLINGTON。
日期 / /

情况正在好转。人们实际上开始对广播产生兴趣，甚至连各协会也振作起来予以关注。这难道不让那些过去两年一直努力在此方向有所成就、且大部分时间显然在孤军奋战的人们感到鼓舞吗？

然而，这里我们有来自布莱恩先生和上海外籍居民协会秘书的投诉，我确信这最终会导致行动。像伍德黑德先生、哈里斯先生和R. G. 麦克唐纳先生这样的人物，一旦着手做事，迟早会有结果，因此我在收到马歇尔先生的来信并得到答复后，又读到一封写给我的信，心中感到某种愉悦和满足。在本期的另一部分可以找到该信件及其回复，现在应该有人就可以采取的措施提出一些建议。

当然，我们可以将XCBL的功率提升（我使用这个名称以便鲍勃能够识别……其正式名称现在是XQHC，虽然我花了近两个月的时间才把字母顺序排对，但现在我已经烂熟于心，无需翻阅《上海呼声》的节目页）到一至五千瓦，但这需要资金，而运营该电台的公司已在电台中投入了约十万美元，因此不愿再投入更多。如果上海的外籍居民能拿出每年10美元的会费来帮助娱乐自己，那么在这方面确实会有所作为，但想到缴纳年会费的人如此之少，使得收支平衡都极其困难，更不用说购买更多的设备和机器来给发射机提供所需的功率提升了。为什么外籍居民协会不能让协会中拥有收音机的每位会员都加入中华广播协会，从而帮助他们支持一项事业？如果因为缺乏这种支持而导致整个电台不得不关闭，他们将非常怀念它。也许有一天，在动荡时期广播电台会非常有用。报纸可能会罢工，或者麻烦可能在最不合时宜的时刻爆发，那时如果没有外国广播电台，我们将身处何地？那些在1926年大罢工期间在国内的人无疑会记得，无线电如何使公众保持良好情绪，让他们了解全国各地的最新消息，使鲍德温先生能够向全国讲话，从而安抚了许多非常焦虑的人。总有一天，我们会非常感激这里的某个广播电台，尽管就我个人而言，希望这种情况不要发生。因此我说，支持中华广播协会，帮助XCBL增强一点实力。

另一种方法，鲍勃，如果你想获得XQHC的良好接收效果，为什么不买一台飞歌（Philco）……现在像你一样……我没有飞歌的利益要维护。我仅仅陈述这一点，因为我每天晚上和白天都能用这台小收音机清晰明确地接收XQHC，没有任何干扰。而且我已经告诉过你，我的英国产收音机做不到这一点。

顺便提一下，上海外国广播电台的情况正在发生变化。各种改善现状的计划正在进行中，但我无权讨论它们或发表任何评论。不过肯定会有结果，尽管我无法确切说明是什么。

如果上海外籍居民协会接手此事，毫无疑问，我们的中国朋友将努力迫使违规电台保持在各自的波段内。问题在于目前还没有对电台的集中管控。应该有这种管控，并且应允许所有租界的警察直接前往违规电台并将其关闭，直到其回到正确的波段。据我所知，规定指出任何电台不得与其他电台相距20千周以内，如果遵守这一规定，一切都会很美好。不幸的是，电台没有刀锋式调谐，因此在某些收音机上，其中一些电台覆盖20至50千周，这使得良好接收成为不可能。当再次坚持晶体控制时，麻烦就会消失，但这完全取决于能否实现某种集中管控。协会能否与南京和上海当权者建立个人联系，让他们会面并创建一个管理机构，该机构有权关闭违规电台一周甚至更长时间，直到它们符合要求？在有人做到这一点之前，空中将会有麻烦。这难道不值得列入下周会议的议程吗？

不幸的是，我不是技术人员，因此无法提出具体建议，但上海有许多人完全有能力做到这一点。贝利斯（Bayliss）在这件事上像黑人一样辛勤工作。既然他已经离开，我建议请各电台的工程师就此主题起草一份备忘录，提交给即将召开的会议。我确信帕克斯先生、盖林先生和约翰·马歇尔可以很容易地提出具有深远影响的建议，但是除非有统一管控，否则建议毫无用处，而这正是必须解决的问题。

上海外籍居民……如果你们希望事情办成，责任就在你们身上，记住“自己动手”的座右铭，全城的中国和外籍居民都会感谢你们。

最后再说一句。除非咨询中国当局并使其完全同情任何提出的计划，否则我确信会导致彻底失败。

ABR
11/24

November 23, 1933    SHANGHAI CALLING

IMPROVING EXISTING BROADCASTING
CONDITIONS    by F. C. M.
The following letter from the Shanghai Foreign Re-
sidents Association and our reply thereto are published
for the information of readers:
China Broadcast Association,    15th Nov. 1933.
113-115 Av. Edouard VII, Local.
DEAR SIR,
The General Committee of the Shanghai Foreign Re-
sidents' Association is looking into the matter of Radio
broadcasting in the area of Shanghai and should like
to be able to make the necessary suggestions to the
different Municipalities of the International Settlement,
French Concession, Greater Shanghai and to the Ministry
of Communication at Nanking, for the purpose of im-
proving the existing conditions, especially with reference
to the interference of one station upon another.
Our Committee would be most obliged if you would
kindly inform me of whatever suggestions you should like
us to take into consideration.
An early reply will be much appreciated.
Yours sincerely,
Shanghai Foreign Residents Association.
W. ADEVEYER.

November 18th, 1933.
The Shanghai Foreign Residents Association,
6 Kiukiang Road, Shanghai.
REFERENCE RADIO BROADCASTING.
DEAR SIR,
With reference to your letter dated 15th November,
1933, we are pleased that your General Committee is
taking an interest in the present congestion of the air.
We would suggest that a meeting be arranged between
your Hon. Secretary and the undersigned, so that you
can be made fully cognizant of the steps which have
been taken with the various bodies.
It is suggested that the offices of the above Associa-
tion would be a suitable meeting place, having all the
necessary data on our files.
Yours truly,
(Signed) J. MARSHALL.
It is highly gratifying to see that at least another
Association is taking up the question of improving broad-
casting in this area. For the past two years, XQHC
officials have been trying to clear up the situation and
whilst a great deal has been accomplished in that direc-
tion, there is still considerable room for improvement.
The interference of XQHC's wave band is definitely bad
at the moment and it would be a real relief to have
someone take charge of the whole situation and rectify
it if possible, so that every station broadcasting would
stay on its own wave band and be at least twenty
kilocycles away from the next station. With such con-
ditions prevailing, any fairly good receiving set would
then have a chance of eliminating all interference.
It will be interesting to note what steps will be
taken by the Foreign Residents' Association when they
have examined the files of XQHC. In any case we wel-
come any suggestions that may come from them regard-
ing the situation.

以下来自上海外籍居民协会的信件及我们的回复现予刊登，供读者参考：
中华广播协会，    1933年11月15日。
爱多亚路113-115号，房间。
尊敬的先生：
上海外籍居民协会总委员会正在调查上海地区的无线电广播事宜，希望能向国际租界、法租界、大上海市政府以及南京交通部提出必要的建议，以改善现有状况，特别是针对一个电台对另一个电台的干扰问题。
如果您能告知我们希望您考虑的任何建议，本委员会将不胜感激。
如蒙早日回复，将不胜感激。

W. ADEVEYER。

1933年11月18日。
上海外籍居民协会，
上海九江路6号。
事由：无线电广播。
尊敬的先生：
关于您1933年11月15日的来信，我们很高兴看到贵总委员会对目前的空中拥堵状况感兴趣。
我们建议安排您的荣誉秘书与 undersigned（签署人）之间举行一次会议，以便让您充分了解已与各机构采取的步骤。
建议以上述协会的办公室作为合适的会议地点，因为我们档案中存有所有必要的数据。
此致，
（签名）J. MARSHALL。
看到至少另一个协会开始关注改善该地区广播的问题，令人非常欣慰。过去两年，XQHC的官员一直试图清理局面，虽然在此方向已取得很大成就，但仍有相当大的改进空间。
目前XQHC波段的干扰确实严重，如果有人能负责整个局面并在可能的情况下加以纠正，使每个广播电台都保持在各自的波段内，并与下一个电台至少相距二十千周，那将是一种真正的解脱。在这种条件下，任何相当好的接收机都将有机会消除所有干扰。
值得注意的是，外籍居民协会在查阅XQHC的档案后将采取什么步骤。无论如何，我们欢迎他们就局势提出的任何建议。

Date Nov. 23, 1933.

Subject (in full) Suggestion for the Improvement of Reception of
Radio Broadcasting - enquiries by Shanghai
Foreign Residents' Association.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Duncan

At a general committee meeting of the Shanghai
Foreign Residents Association it was suggested that, in
regard to the numerous complaints heard in connection with
the poor reception of radio broadcasting in Shanghai, a
Sub-Committee be appointed to go into the matter with a
view to improving the existing conditions. Accordingly
Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffe, Vice Chairman of the Association and
Mr. Synnerberg, representing the Finnish Association were
appointed. Both Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffe and Synnerberg have
canvassed likely persons for suggestions but so far
nothing of a helpful nature has been learned.
In an interview with Mr. Synnerberg, he expressed
the opinion that it should be an easy matter for the S.M.C.
to control the Broadcasting stations in the Settlement and
with the cooperation of the French and Chinese authorities
the matter of interference of one station upon another could
be eliminated. It will be seen from the foregoing that
Mr. Synnerberg is not conversant with the difficulties
facing the Council in this matter and it is unlikely that
suggestions, if any, put forward by the Sub-Committee of
the Foreign Residents Association will prove of value in
assisting to bring about a satisfactory arrangement in the
matter.

主题（全称） 关于改善无线电广播接收效果的建议——上海外侨协会之问询。

由特别股督察长邓肯（Duncan）呈报并转递

在上海外侨协会（Shanghai Foreign Residents Association）的一次全体委员会会议上，有人提议，鉴于有关上海无线电广播接收效果不佳的投诉屡见不鲜，应任命一个小组委员会对此事进行调查，以期改善现状。据此，该协会副主席德奥克西翁·德吕夫先生（Mr. d'Auxion de Ruffe）和代表芬兰人协会（Finnish Association）的辛纳伯格先生（Mr. Synnerberg）获任。德奥克西翁·德吕夫先生和辛纳伯格先生均向可能提供意见的人士征询了建议，但迄今未获得任何有益的信息。
在与辛纳伯格先生的一次面谈中，他表示认为，工部局（S.M.C.）管控租界内的广播电台应当是易事，且若能得到法方及中方当局的配合，各电台相互干扰的问题便可消除。从前文可以看出，辛纳伯格先生并不熟悉工部局在此事上面临的困难，因此，外侨协会小组委员会即便提出建议，恐怕也难以对促成此事的圆满解决提供有价值的帮助。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 13, 1933
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
N. D 4778
D. 19 - 4 - 33

Local Foreign Residents
Form Association

International Group Appoints Committee For Purpose Of Safeguarding Interests; Greater Co-operation Among Foreigners Sought

Formed for the purpose of wider co-operation and unity among foreigners of all nationalities in Shanghai, the Shanghai Foreign Residents' Association has announced its policy and the names of members of a Provisional General Committee in a circular issued to prospective members. The contents of the circular follow:

With a view to securing greater unity and co-operation among the various nationalities represented in Shanghai and promoting the future peace, security and prosperity of this great city, a number of foreign residents have met together during the past year to consider the various questions which so vitally affect the interests of Shanghai Residents.

This group, which mainly consists of representatives of various National Organizations, Chambers of Commerce and Residents' Associations, has come to the conclusion that the only way of ensuring effective expression of the views of Foreign Residents of Shanghai is by forming a Foreign Residents' Association, and this Association has accordingly been formed.

Under the existing municipal regulations only a small proportion of the foreign residents possesses electoral rights and probably 70 per cent., or more have no means of expressing their views on matters in which their welfare is deeply concerned.

Protection Of Interests

The object of this Association is simply the protection of the interests of Foreign residents in Shanghai, and it has been decided that every foreigner, resident in Shanghai, who has attained the age of 18 years, and signifies that he is in sympathy with its aims and who subscribes the nominal membership fee of One Dollar annually, shall be eligible for membership.

One often hears the statement made that we are not consulted about matters which vitally affect our interests; but so long as we have no organization through which we can make known our views we cannot complain that these views are not taken into consideration.

The Shanghai Foreign Residents' Association proposes to study every problem which concerns the interests of foreigners residing in Shanghai and China generally, especially such problems as relate to the Government and Administration of Shanghai and the promotion of Peace, Security and Prosperity in the Shanghai Area.

Joint Action

One of the advantages of this Association is that it will be able to co-ordinate the activities of the existing National Associations. Frequently when one of the National Associations takes action and makes representations to its Home Government in regard to a matter concerning the welfare of its nationals, it is found that this matter affects the welfare of all foreign residents in Shanghai, and it would frequently be desirable to take joint action by all foreigners in Shanghai rather than that the burden should rest on one particular National Association.

Further, since, in the final analysis, the interests of all residents of Shanghai—Chinese and Foreign—are identical, it is hoped that there will be close co-operation between the Shanghai Foreign Residents' Association and the Chinese Ratepayers' Association or other representative Chinese bodies.

A body such as the Shanghai Foreign Residents' Association will be in a position to make representations to the Diplomatic and Consular Bodies and the League of Nations in connection with matters affecting the welfare of Shanghai, and it is almost certain that serious questions affecting the welfare of this city will come up for consideration in the near, if not the immediate, future.

Local Affairs

On the other hand, local affairs and the interests of the foreign community as a whole will not be considered from the angle of any particular country, but will be studied entirely from the standpoint of the resident in Shanghai. While it is natural that each national association should be guided by its own national policy, the policy of this association will be conceived entirely in the light of an understanding that Shanghai's interests are not national but international, and that unless this characteristic feature is established and maintained there is no likelihood of our joint interests ever being envisaged in the right perspective or efficiently protected in a permanent manner.

It has already been stated that the Provisional Committee of the Foreign Residents' Association is mainly composed of members nominated by the various National Associations and Chambers of Commerce and while it is essential that every nationality should be adequately represented on the Committee and a proper proportion of national representation be maintained, the Committee hopes to devise a practicable plan whereby a definite number of members of the Committee will be elected by the members of the Association who will thus have a direct voice in the management of its affairs.

For the current year the present Provisional Committee will continue to act and before the end of the year a form of Constitution will be drawn up to be submitted to members of the Association for adoption.

It is obvious that the influence that the Shanghai Foreign Residents' Association will be able to exert must depend on the strength of its membership and the support it receives from Shanghai Foreign Residents of all nationalities.

Provisional Committee

本地外侨
组建协会

国际团体任命委员会以维护利益；寻求外侨间更紧密合作

上海外侨协会旨在促进上海所有国籍外侨之间更广泛的合作与团结，已在发给潜在会员的通函中宣布其政策及临时全体委员会成员名单。通函内容如下：

为确保上海各外籍族群之间更大的团结与合作，并促进这座伟大城市未来的和平、安全与繁荣，过去一年里，一批外侨聚集在一起，探讨严重影响上海居民利益的各种问题。

该团体主要由各国组织、商会及居民协会的代表组成，其结论是，确保上海外侨观点得到有效表达的唯一途径是成立一个外侨协会，该协会由此成立。

根据现行市政规章，只有一小部分外侨拥有选举权，可能有70%或更多的外侨无法在深切关乎其福祉的事务上发表意见。

保护利益

本协会的宗旨仅仅是保护在上海的外侨利益。经决定，凡居住在上海、年满18岁、表示赞同本协会目标并每年缴纳一美元名义会费的外国人，均有资格成为会员。

人们常听到这样的说法：在严重影响我们利益的事务上，无人征求我们的意见；但是，只要我们没有组织来发表观点，我们就不能抱怨这些观点未被考虑。

上海外侨协会拟研究每一个涉及居住在上海及中国各地外侨利益的问题，特别是那些与上海政府及管理、以及促进上海地区和平、安全与繁荣相关的问题。

联合行动

本协会的优势之一在于能够协调现有各国协会的活动。通常，当某一国协会就关乎其国民福祉的事项采取行动并向其本国政府提出交涉时，会发现该事项影响上海所有外侨的福祉，此时由上海所有外侨采取联合行动往往比让负担落在某一个特定国家协会身上更为可取。

此外，既然归根结底，上海所有居民——华人与外人——的利益是一致的，希望上海外侨协会能与华人纳税会或其他代表性华人团体保持密切合作。

像上海外侨协会这样的机构，将就影响上海福祉的事项向外交使团、领事团及国际联盟提出交涉。几乎可以肯定，影响本市福祉的严重问题将在不久的将来，若非即刻，也会提上议事日程。

本地事务

另一方面，本地事务及整个外侨社群的利益不会从任何特定国家的角度加以考量，而是完全从上海居民的立场进行研究。虽然各国协会受其本国政策引导是自然的，但本协会的政策将完全基于这样一种认识来制定：上海的利益不是国家性的，而是国际性的；除非确立并维持这一特征，否则我们的共同利益就不太可能被正确地看待或得到有效的永久保护。

前已述及，外侨协会临时委员会主要由各国协会和商会提名的成员组成。虽然必须确保每个国籍在委员会中有充分的代表并保持适当的国籍比例，但委员会希望制定一个切实可行的计划，即由协会会员选举确定数量的委员会成员，从而使会员对其事务管理拥有直接发言权。

本年度，现任临时委员会将继续履职，年底前将起草章程草案，提交协会会员通过。

显而易见，上海外侨协会所能发挥的影响力取决于其会员力量以及来自上海所有国籍外侨的支持。
